Kimi K3.1 Pro review · Stefan (spatial-reasoning 3D tests, four models)

Kimi K3.1 Pro: 3D Gauntlet

Kimi K3.1 Pro vs DeepSeek 4.1 (open weights) vs Gemini 4 and Opus 5.5 (paid). Kimi and DeepSeek were run inside the Claude Code harness (he notes Kimi is lazier in its own Kimi Code harness, but cheaper there). Tests are purely 3D and spatial: no 3D-asset generation except in the whale test. Host has tested Kimi K3 since August and says K3.1 Pro is clearly better than K3.

Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cxxGMz-YXU0. Every image is a frame grabbed from that video; click its timestamp to jump there. Figures are as spoken in the video (auto-transcript), not independently re-measured.

Host sentiment
Best open model here; Opus still ahead
Opus 5.5best on most visual tests
Kimibeat Gemini 4 repeatedly; best controls on tiny planets
  • Enthusiastic about open weights, honest about the gap. Opens with "Open source AI is back" and closes that open models are catching up, which will pressure big labs on price. Opus 5.5 (and GPT-6 Astra) still perform better.
  • Kimi consistently landed ahead of DeepSeek 4.1 and, more often than not, ahead of Gemini 4, which he treats as the biggest disappointment of the video. He says Kimi and DeepSeek were easier to work with than Gemini 4.
  • Positive moments: Kimi chose the harder, more-fold origami approach (second place), produced the cleanest controls on tiny planets, and was "less broken" on pinball logic.
  • Negative moments: White House rooms with gaps and floating objects, a lazy parts-on-the-ground Kawasaki assembly, an underwhelming whale flip, and a dragon rig that looked like a step backward vs K3 (better motion, worse rigging).
  • On cost he is puzzled that API cost lands closer to Opus than expected because the $0.20/M cache-read price is the same as Opus. Final line: Kimi is about five times cheaper than GPT-6 Astra; locally hosted (weights promised for November 4) cost stops mattering.

Tests and results

01Warm-upOpus

Apollo 11 lunar descent (20 s)

Task

Render a 20-second Apollo 11 landing (Claude suggested it because the lab is Moonshot).

Result

Kimi: few details but works, "okayish". DeepSeek added a miniature Earth. Gemini 4 similar, slightly better. Opus: clearly best, telemetry numbers, particles, accurate landing.

02Setupn/a

API cost and Claude Code setup

Task

How Kimi and DeepSeek were wired into Claude Code (a "claude kimi" command with effort settings).

Result

Kimi's cost lands closer to Opus than its sticker suggests because cache reads cost $0.20/M on both. Kimi is lazier inside Kimi Code than inside Claude Code, which forces more iteration.

033D sceneOpus

White House 3D exploration

Task

Explorable White House with room cutaways, exploded/section views.

Result

Kimi: better than K3, but poor placement, big gaps, objects floating, ambient-occlusion issue. DeepSeek: nicer interiors, broken controls. Gemini 4: same box-fitting problems, "really disappointing". Kimi roughly on Gemini's level. Opus: grounded building, waving flag, no wall gaps, detailed top floor.

043D animationOpus, Kimi 2nd

Origami folding

Task

Animate paper folding into an origami shape in 3D.

Result

Inherently hard (thin-plane clipping). Kimi chose the harder multi-fold approach, some z-fighting. DeepSeek: "lazy origami". Gemini: clipping, spent 4 h and 5M tokens. Opus: same approach as Kimi with fewer visual issues. Host ranks Kimi second; Kimi was faster than the others.

05RiggingK3 (older)

Dragon rigging rematch (K3 vs K3.1 Pro)

Task

Re-run of an earlier test Kimi K3 won; only Kimi versions compared.

Result

K3.1 Pro has more movement but worse rigging: one leg rigged, another leg floating in the air, leg issues. Host: "a bit disappointing", looks like a step back.

063D assemblyOpus

Kawasaki H2 assembly

Task

Assemble the motorcycle from parts in an animation.

Result

Kimi: parts laid on the ground then joined ("lazy approach"), runs but lacks detail. DeepSeek: same idea, lower quality. Gemini 4: broken render. Opus: many more parts, clearly better though not its best.

073D animationOpus

Whale jump (mascot shot)

Task

Whale leaps from the water toward the moon; generated 3D models allowed via his APIs.

Result

Kimi: odd side-flip, weak dynamics. DeepSeek: no flip. Gemini 4: broken mesh (unmerged vertices), disqualified. Opus: matched his reference shot, went into the thumbnail. He notes Kimi wasn't using cache this time.

083D animationUndecided (Kimi > Gemini)

Car-to-robot transform

Task

Transformers-style car morphing into a robot.

Result

Kimi: GTA San Andreas-style car, transform works. DeepSeek: simpler shapes. Gemini 4: ugly pieces; host says Kimi beat Gemini here. Opus: merges well but empty streets; he left the call to viewers.

09GameMixed (Kimi on logic)

Pinball game

Task

Windows-classic-style pinball.

Result

Kimi: playable, least broken logic, visually weaker. DeepSeek: surprisingly good, some logic errors. Gemini 4: ball stuck, unplayable. Opus: ball slows and disappears. Visually Opus and DeepSeek best; Kimi best logic.

10GameKimi (controls)

Tiny planets

Task

Jump between small planets with their own gravity.

Result

Kimi: legless player, jumping awkward but works; cleanest controls of the four. DeepSeek: legs, nice concept, near-impossible targeting. Gemini 4: lags, terrible controls. Opus: appealing visuals and legs, controls inverted and broken. Kimi was the most expensive on this test.

Built from the video transcript and frames extracted from the video itself. Model names, prices and scores are reported as the host stated them on 2026-10.
